calls.head: Tilted ice, toward the Maple Leafs’ net
calls.body: The Avalanche have been the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Maple Leafs one of the worst. Expect the Avalanche to spend more of the night in the Maple Leafs’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

surprises.head: A rough night for Mackenzie Blackwood
surprises.body: Blackwood allowed 5 goals on 22 shots, worth 2.2 expected goals: 2.8 more than expected. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 25 starts.

surprises.head: Toronto won against the run of play
surprises.body: With chances like these, Colorado would win about 70 games in 100. Toronto won anyway.

story.head: Nylander reaches 700 points with a five-point night as the Maple Leafs beat the Avalanche
paras: Nick Blankenburg made his Maple Leafs debut, after playing for the Avalanche. Blankenburg got the scoring started for the Maple Leafs early in the first, but Nathan MacKinnon tied it 1-1 for Colorado midway through the period. The Maple Leafs’ Chris Tanev left in the first period and didn’t return. The next day, he was placed on injured reserve with an upper-body injury. MacKinnon scored again late in the period to put the Avalanche ahead 2-1. The second period was a wild one. William Nylander tied it up for Toronto on the power play early in the period. Brock Nelson put the Avalanche back ahead 3-2 midway through the period, and that was all they would get. Nylander struck again less than five minutes later to tie it 3-3, his 700th NHL point, and Easton Cowan gave the Maple Leafs the lead 46 seconds later. Auston Matthews made it 5-3 on the power play with just under eight minutes left, and he scored again into the empty net with 39 seconds left. Nylander added three assists for a five-point night, and Matthews had two assists for a four-point night.

The score flatters the Maple Leafs: the Avalanche had the better of the chances. Replay those chances a hundred times and the Avalanche win about seven in ten. Sergei Bobrovsky was the difference, stopping 30 of 33. Mackenzie Blackwood allowed five goals on 22 shots for the Avalanche.
The Maple Leafs killed all five Avalanche power plays. The Leafs improved to 3-2-1 and climbed to fourth in the Atlantic, while the Avalanche fell to 3-2-0, slipping to fourth in the Central.

items.text: William Nylander passed Frank Mahovlich and George Armstrong for seventh on the Maple Leafs’ all-time goals list, with 297.
Nicolas Roy played his first game against Toronto since leaving.
Nathan MacKinnon extended his point streak against Toronto to seven games.
Cale Makar extended his point streak against Toronto to six games.
